items.notes: Quote: 'this function's own repair `ZAddNX` errors (timeout, reset, cluster MOVED/ASK) and the result is discarded. ... The member is never restored'. The fact is true (l.250 is unchecked). go-redis follows MOVED/ASK redirects internally, so naming those as terminal errors overstates the case, but timeouts and resets are possible. Register non_defects: 'Request cancellation or a client timeout can abandon the restore after ZREM landed (#10743 item 3)' is ruled 'Non-material narrow hypothetical: harm needs a concurrent same-path recreate inside the GET->EXISTS window plus a cancellation or timeout between two back-to-back commands'. This item is that same narrow hypothetical, so it is non-material. It does not identify GT-s1's replica-routed GET/EXISTS mechanism, and a retry of ZAddNX does not address GT-s1.

Quote: 'The pre-existing logical-expiry branch ... also discards its Del/ZRem results without checking, unchanged by this diff and outside its scope.' This is accurate (clone l.216-217) and pre-existing. It is a hygiene observation, so it is non-material.

Quote: 'this `ZAddNX`'s result is never checked. If it errors, the member stays removed while the value stays live'; Fix: 'Check the `ZAddNX` error and log it'. The fact is true (l.250 discards the result). Register non_defects: 'Request cancellation or a client timeout can abandon the restore after ZREM landed (#10743 item 3)' is ruled 'Non-material narrow hypothetical: harm needs a concurrent same-path recreate inside the GET->EXISTS window plus a cancellation or timeout between two back-to-back commands'. This item is that same concurrent-recreate plus failed-restore hypothetical, so it is non-material. The proposed logging would not restore the member in any case. The item does not identify GT-s1's replica-routing mechanism.

Quote: '`DeleteFolderChildren` deletes each child's value key directly from the ZSET's members without ever `ZRem`-ing them ... unrelated to this diff'. This is accurate (clone l.145-170: members are iterated and values DEL'd with no ZRem; DeleteEntry l.121 DELs the path's own index key). The item describes pre-existing code, asserts no defect, and proposes no fix, so it is non-material.

Quote: 'the restoring `ZAddNX` call's own error is never checked. ... If that one write fails (a transient Redis error), the member stays removed even though its value exists'. The fact is true: clone universal_redis_store.go:250 discards the ZAddNX result. Register non_defects: 'Request cancellation or a client timeout can abandon the restore after ZREM landed (#10743 item 3)' is ruled 'Non-material narrow hypothetical: harm needs a concurrent same-path recreate inside the GET->EXISTS window plus a cancellation or timeout between two back-to-back commands'. This item's scenario (concurrent recreate plus a failed restore write) is that same narrow hypothetical, so it is non-material. It does not identify GT-s1: it does not mention replica-routed GET/EXISTS, a lagging replica, or a positive-but-wrong EXISTS=0 under routeByLatency/useReadOnly. Checking or retrying the ZAddNX error would not address GT-s1.

Quote: 'TestRemoveOrphanedDirectoryListMemberKeepsRecreatedEntry only exercises keyPrefix=""'. The core claim is true (test file l.106-107). The comparison is partly wrong: the TTL test at l.123-124 also uses only newTestStore(t, ""), so it does not loop over "sw:" as the item implies. This is a test-coverage hygiene remark with no product consequence, so it is non-material.

Quote: 'The new orphan-removal call is unreachable for super-large directories: InsertEntry skips ZAddNX and DeleteEntry skips ZRem when isSuperLargeDirectory is true, so `<dir>\x00` never exists for them'. This repeats the PR body's own observation and asserts no defect or consequence. It is accurate for directories that were super-large from the start (clone universal_redis_store.go:63-65, 132-134). Per the register, the code is reachable for directories converted later, but that case is also ruled non-material. No fix is proposed. It is an observation below the threshold, and it does not touch GT-s1 (replica-routed GET/EXISTS).

Quote: 'a directory reconfigured to super-large after already holding index members would still have a stray member re-added by the repair path if a value reappears during the ZRem→EXISTS window — a narrow edge case'. The mechanism is accurate: the restore at l.250 has no isSuperLargeDirectory guard. The only effect is re-adding a member that was present before the ZREM, so the net state is unchanged. The register rules the super-large-directory legacy-member objection non-material, and the reviewer calls this a narrow edge case. Nothing here concerns replica routing (GT-s1).

Quote: 'a DeleteEntry or the sibling expiry branch deletes that same value ... The trailing ZAddNX re-adds the member for a value that is once again absent, reintroducing exactly the orphan this change removes, until the next listing repeats the whole cycle.' The interleaving is possible: EXISTS sees the value, a DeleteEntry runs DEL then a no-op ZRem, and ZAddNX re-adds the member. The consequence the reviewer states is only a stale orphan member that the next listing cleans up. That is the direction the PR deliberately accepts (a stale member rather than a lost one), and at the merge-base orphans persisted forever. The effect is transient and benign, so it is non-material. The item does not concern replica routing (GT-s1).

Quote: 'The `glog.V(0)` skip log at universal_redis_store.go:206 still fires once for every orphan the new cleanup removes'. This is true: clone l.206 logs before the ErrNotFound branch. The register non_defects rule 'glog.V(0) logs every missing member' pre-existing hygiene, so it is non-material.
